messages:
julia.csm: FYI — early adopter ACME hitting intermittent 429s during SDK init when traffic is routed through their edge proxy. Happens on spikes during our onboarding load test. Logs pasted below, can we triage?

mike.sdk: Thanks — can you paste the exact request/response log? Are the 429s coming from Redwood or the customer's proxy?

julia.csm: Paste from their dev:
```
2026-03-18T14:22:33Z INFO outbound request id=abc123 host=api.redwood.ai status=429 body="rate limit exceeded" x-request-id=rx-9f2
2026-03-18T14:22:34Z INFO outbound request id=abc124 host=api.redwood.ai status=200
2026-03-18T14:22:35Z INFO outbound request id=abc125 host=api.redwood.ai status=429 body="rate limit exceeded" x-request-id=rx-9f3
```
They say responses are sporadic; happens only when proxy is enabled.

sarah.infra: Two quick hypotheses: (1) The proxy pools upstream connections so many customer SDK clients appear to come from one IP — triggers per-IP rate caps. (2) Proxy may be dropping/stripping `Authorization` or `X-Client-ID` headers on retries, causing some requests to be unauthenticated and rejected.

mike.sdk: Good call. Our rate limiting logic is per-api-key and per-ip fallback. If all traffic is NATed behind the proxy IP, the per-IP path will kick in. Do we have `Retry-After` or `x-rate-limit-*` headers in the 429 responses from our side?

julia.csm: They captured this from the client:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2026 14:22:33 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 14
```
So looks like our 429s with standard headers.

devon.eng: If Retry-After present our SDK will back off, but bursts during init still fail. Two actionable items: (A) confirm the proxy is not reusing a single API key or connection pooling incorrectly, (B) short-term we can raise per-account burst allowance for ACME while they roll out a proxy config change.

sarah.infra: For (A) ask them to verify they are forwarding `X-Forwarded-For` and not rewriting `Authorization`. Also check if their proxy does transparent retries on 502/timeout and resends with different auth header — that can trigger auth errors.

mike.sdk: Suggest a small repro snippet they can run without the proxy to show success. Also a proxy-only run to show failure so we can compare headers. Example curl they can run:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines/text/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Then run same through proxy and `-v` to dump headers.

julia.csm: ACME did the repro. When going direct -> 0 429s. Through proxy -> ~1 in 10 requests 429, coming from same upstream IP. They confirmed `X-Forwarded-For` is present but has a single value from proxy.

devon.eng: That's classic NAT/coalescing. Two options: (1) Have them enable client IP passthrough (preserve original IP in X-Forwarded-For chain) so our per-ip fallback is less aggressive, (2) we add an allowlist exception for their account's burst pattern while they fix proxy.

mike.sdk: Operationally we prefer (1) since it prevents future surprises. For short term (2) is fine. If we do (2) I'll need an account id and expected QPS and burst window.

julia.csm: ACME account: acct_0009, expected steady qps=15, burst to 90 for 30s during startup. They can change proxy in ~24-48 hours.

ops-bot: Ticket CS-PRIORITY-781 created by julia.csm: Temporary burst raise for acct_0009 to 90 qps for 30s window. Assigned to devon.eng. ETA: 4 hours.

devon.eng: I will implement a temporary policy change. Will also add a log flag to show whether requests matched api-key vs ip bucket for a sample window so we can confirm.

sarah.infra: Also ask ACME to enable connection-level keepalives and disable aggressive connection multiplexing across many clients if possible. That reduces the effective IP fan-in.

mike.sdk: Added a small SDK tweak we can patch quickly: on init, if we detect `429` responses from same IP and a configured `proxy_detect=true`, SDK will increase jittered backoff and spread startup retries over 10s. I'll open a PR for a patch release.

julia.csm: Great. I'll schedule a 30-min call with ACME for tomorrow 10am PT to walk them through proxy config and confirm the temporary burst lift. I'll follow up after the call. :thumbsup:

devon.eng: Temporary policy applied. I'll post logs when I have sample data.

ops-bot: CS-PRIORITY-781 updated: status=done, note="temporary burst rule active until 2026-03-20T01:00:00Z"

mike.sdk: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/478 — adds proxy-detection backoff.

julia.csm: Thanks everyone — follow-up: re-check in 24 hrs and confirm renewal health unchanged.

sarah.infra: If after proxy changes we still see 429s, we'll review per-account token scoping and whether their key is shared across multiple services.

julia.csm: Closing loop here: ACME rolled proxy change, 0 429s in 24h smoke test. Renewal health green. Closing thread. :tada:
